clue.text: Title for chap guarding queen, in a way

indicators.note: a guard stands on each side of the thing protected, so the title wraps round the queen

parts.note: Mr is the usual courtesy title for a man
Queen Anne, the last Stuart monarch

explanation.surface: A man's title somehow keeps watch over a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link word; the definition is 'a way', in the sense of a fashion of doing something.
explanation.definitionFit: Manner and way are synonyms for the fashion in which something is done.

clue.text: Size of big explosion turning up no precious stone

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: something that is not a gem: NOT A GEM

explanation.surface: A jeweller's disappointment at finding nothing valuable after a big blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reads NOT A GEM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaton is a unit of explosive power, a million tons of TNT, used to size nuclear blasts.

clue.text: New song raised money in Africa

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means lifted up, so the song is written bottom to top

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A new song is put up to bring in cash somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ARIA into AIRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The naira is the currency of Nigeria.

clue.text: Part of circuit chosen, then travelled

parts.note: elect as an adjective means chosen, as in president-elect
rode means travelled on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: A racing driver is picked for the track and then drives it.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a conductor through which current enters or leaves part of an electrical circuit.

clue.text: Work in parts arranged for each of Queen's musicians

indicators.note: the work goes inside the reshuffled parts
parts that are arranged are put into a new order, signalling a reshuffle of those letters

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: An orchestral work is split into parts and scored for the band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen here is the rock band, not a monarch; 'arranged' reshuffles the five letters into PSTAR, and the work sits inside after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Each member of the rock band Queen is a famous pop musician, a celebrity of the charts.

clue.text: Anticipate publicity proclamation

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity
an edict is an official proclamation

explanation.surface: A press office expects a public announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: To predict something is to foresee or anticipate it before it happens.

clue.text: Plain maiden taken in by old man

indicators.note: the maiden is taken inside the old man's word

parts.note: old man is slang for father, so papa
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: An unadorned young woman is given a home by an elderly gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Plain looks like an adjective about the maiden, but it is a noun: a grassy plain.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampa is the great grassy plain of Argentina.

clue.text: Encountered in English and French articles music associated with 20, say

indicators.note: the meeting word goes inside the pair of articles

parts.note: the is the English definite article
une is the French feminine indefinite article
met means encountered

explanation.surface: Bumping into grammar words in two languages while humming a programme's music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' serves both languages: THE and UNE. 20 is EAST END, giving the British soap EastEnders, famous for its opening music.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature piece of music that introduces a television programme such as a soap.

clue.text: Produce sound reflections contributing to free choice

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Making noises bounce back helps someone decide freely.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound again, as an echo does, is to make the reflection of a noise repeat.

clue.text: Old stringed instrument on sign

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a beck is a nod or gesture, a sign, as in beck and call

explanation.surface: An antique fiddle carries a label.
explanation.definitionFit: The rebeck is a medieval bowed instrument, an ancestor of the violin.

clue.text: Queen invariably accepted by African country? Not altogether

indicators.note: the word for always is taken inside the shortened country
the country is not given in full, losing its final letter

parts.note: Guinea is a country in West Africa
ever means always, invariably

explanation.surface: A queen is always welcome in an African state, though not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not altogether' drops only the final letter of the country, leaving GUINE to hold the word for always.
explanation.definitionFit: Guinevere was the legendary queen of King Arthur.

clue.text: Queen Mother meeting first lady

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: The Queen Mother meets the US president's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Mother' looks like one phrase, but Queen is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Maeve was a warrior queen of Connacht in Irish legend.

clue.text: The Queen, say, to perfection welcoming head of state

indicators.note: welcoming takes a guest inside, so the phrase wraps round the letter

parts.note: to a T means exactly, to perfection

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word state

explanation.surface: Royalty is perfectly suited to receiving a visiting head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives S, which 'welcoming' puts inside TO A T.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising glasses to the Queen is a classic example of a toast at a dinner.

clue.text: Queen briefly appearing in 9, 16 and 27

parts.note: the royal cypher ER, short for Regina with the monarch's name, appears as a pair of letters in the solutions to 9, 16 and 27

explanation.walkthrough: GUINEVERE, RELAPSERS and CATHERINE each contain ER, the cypher of Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth II's monogram ER is the abbreviation of Elizabeth Regina, so the queen appears in short form.

clue.text: Doctor knew half of royals — that includes Queens

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are rearranged
half of takes the first three of the six letters of royals

explanation.surface: A physician knew half the royal family, Queens among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives ROY; 'Doctor' rearranges KNEW plus ROY. Queens is one of the city's five boroughs.
explanation.definitionFit: Queens is a borough of this American city, so the city contains it.

clue.text: Hit with something contentious in part of foundation

parts.note: to whale is to beat or thrash
a bone of contention is something argued over

explanation.surface: A blow struck amid a dispute about building foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: A foundation here is a foundation garment such as a corset, once stiffened with strips of baleen.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleen strips from whales stiffened corsets, the foundation garments of the past.

clue.text: Necklace from ancestor queen acquired

indicators.note: the necklace is acquired from inside the words that follow, a run across their boundary

explanation.surface: A necklace that a queen took from her ancestor.
explanation.definitionFit: A torque, also spelt torc, is a twisted metal neck ring worn by ancient Celts.

clue.text: Real disruption perturbed press — their complaints get worse again

indicators.note: disruption throws a word into disorder, here the word real
perturbed means thrown into confusion, so the word press is rearranged

explanation.surface: Genuine upheaval rattles the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disruption' turns REAL into RELA and 'perturbed' turns PRESS into PSERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Patients who relapse fall ill again after seeming to recover, so their illnesses worsen.

clue.text: Queens in East spotted a king going west

indicators.note: in an across answer going west means reading right to left

parts.note: seen means spotted, noticed
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: Eastern royals were seen as a king travelled westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' reverses SEEN A R in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranees, or ranis, are Hindu queens or the wives of rajas in India.

clue.text: Mixed with cider, as required for cocktail

indicators.note: mixed suggests the letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A bartender stirs cider in as the recipe demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' rearranges CIDER and AS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Queens, for example, on being embraced by merry monarch

indicators.note: the cricket side is hugged inside the king's name

parts.note: Old King Cole was a merry old soul in the nursery rhyme
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: Royal women being hugged by a jolly king.
explanation.walkthrough: Queens' College is in Cambridge and Queen's College in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Queens' is one of the colleges of Cambridge University.

clue.text: Keen to include a measure that's shrewd

indicators.note: the wailing word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to keen is to wail in mourning, to cry
ft, a foot, is a measure of length

explanation.surface: Eager to put a measurement in, a sharp operator.
explanation.walkthrough: Keen looks like an adjective meaning eager; it is the verb meaning to wail.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafty and shrewd both describe someone cunning and clever in dealings.

clue.text: Part of our capital retrieved from enterprise as ten dividends

indicators.note: retrieved from says the answer is recovered from a run of letters inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A London borough's investments yield tenfold returns.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is a district of London, the British capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The East End is the eastern district of London.

clue.text: Embargo what French put in vessel

parts.note: to bar something is to ban or embargo it
que is French for what

explanation.surface: A trade ban on what the French loaded onto a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A barque is a sailing ship with three or more masts.

clue.text: Queen I expelled from Mediterranean city

indicators.note: expelled means thrown out, so the letter I is removed from the city

parts.note: Alexandria is the Egyptian port on the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A queen says she was thrown out of a Mediterranean port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expelled from' removes the I named in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandra was the Danish princess who became queen of Edward VII.

clue.text: Pale in colour, like one kind of crustacean

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as
a hen is a female lobster or crab

explanation.surface: Something pale is compared to a shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: Hen is not just a bird: it also names a female lobster.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes the grey pallor of ash, so pale.

clue.text: In hand, bridge partners spot queens, potentially

parts.note: a paw is a jokey word for a hand
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Card players with hands spot future royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: A pawn reaching the far side of a chessboard can be promoted, usually to a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pawns may be promoted to queens on reaching the last rank.

clue.text: Noise made by fans, leading West Ham in rare recovery

indicators.note: leading letters are the first of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Football supporters roar as West Ham stage a rare comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: Fans look like football supporters but are electric fans that buzz.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirr is the continuous buzzing hum of rotating blades.

clue.text: Queen awfully hot, it was said

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The Queen complained that it was dreadfully hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' turns HOT into OTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoth is the archaic past tense of quethe, meaning said.

clue.text: Film player capturing the rook or queen

indicators.note: capturing takes pieces inside, so the actor's name surrounds them

parts.note: Michael Caine is a famous film actor
taken as written
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess game played on screen: take the rook or the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess words mislead: the rook is just a letter, and the film player is the actor Michael, who swallows the article and that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine is a queen's name, borne by Catherine the Great and Catherine of Aragon.

clue.text: French queen's refusal received by English king

indicators.note: the refusal is received inside the other letters

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's legendary king
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A French queen's rejection reaches an English king.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of queen's is a link meaning 'has'; Lear counts as an English king because Shakespeare set him in ancient Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor of Aquitaine was queen of France before marrying Henry II of England.

clue.text: A short step for queen going from one European country to another

definitions.text: queen going from one European country to another

indicators.note: short means the step loses its final letter

parts.note: a stride is a long step

explanation.surface: A small step for a queen moving between countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts STRIDE to STRID. Astrid, a Swedish princess, became queen of the Belgians.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Astrid was born in Sweden and became queen consort of Belgium.
